mainEntity.name: How much does a Mitsubishi L200 2.4 DI-D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mitsubishi L200 2.4 DI-D engine replacement typically costs £800-£1,800 for a used unit, £1,800-£2,800 for reconditioned, and £2,800-£4,200 for a rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty. Specialist fitting costs add £600-£900.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mitsubishi L200 2.4 DI-D a reliable engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 4N15 engine has known issues, particularly with exhaust manifold cracking, DPF regeneration problems, and turbocharger failure. Mitsubishi has released updated parts (manifold 1555B029) to address these issues. With regular maintenance and preventative updates, many units prove durable.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mitsubishi L200 2.4 DI-D have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 4N15 2.4 DI-D engine uses a timing chain, not a belt. The timing chain has 108 links and is a simplex (single row) closed chain. Timing chain kits, including the chain, tensioner, and guides, are available for the 4N15 engine.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of exhaust manifold failure on an L200 2.4 DI-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include loss of power, engine entering limp mode, audible exhaust leakage/hissing, and a check engine light. The manifold cracking issue is well-documented, with reports of failure before 40,000km. If you experience these symptoms, have the manifold inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi L200 2.4 DI-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: With 2015-2025 L200 2.4 DI-D values ranging from £6,000-£25,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,800-£4,200 represents 15-40% of the vehicle's value. Given the L200's strong commercial and 4x4 retained values, a rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty is generally a viable investment.

mainEntity.name: What power output does the 4N15 engine have?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 4N15 engine is available in two power outputs. The standard version produces 154PS (113kW) and 380Nm of torque, while the high-output version produces 181PS (133kW) and 430Nm of torque. The 4N15 is a 2.4L 4-cylinder DOHC turbocharged diesel with common rail injection.

historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi L200 2.4 DI-D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mitsubishi L200 2.4 DI-D was introduced in 2015 as the replacement for the older 2.5L 4D56 engine, bringing a modern, lighter, all-aluminium 2.4L diesel to the L200 range. This engine, designated 4N15, is a joint development between Mitsubishi Motors Corporation and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and is part of the MIVEC engine family.

milestones.description: L200 launches with 4N15 2.4 DI-D engine, replacing 4D56
2025 - 4N15 offered in two power outputs: 154PS (113kW) and 181PS (133kW)
2026 onward - New generation L200 introduced with updated 4N16 engine

items.title: 2.4L DI-D Diesel (2015-2025)
items.commonFailure: The 4N15 engine has several known issues. Exhaust manifold cracking (part number 1555A843) is a well-documented failure, with reports of failure before 40,000km. This is believed to be caused by an undersized cooling system working at its limit, causing the manifold to operate at excessive temperatures. Mitsubishi has released an updated manifold (part number 1555B029) as a countermeasure. Additionally, DPF regeneration issues cause frequent warning lights and rapid oil level rise, particularly in urban use. Turbocharger failure (1515A417) also affects the 4N15, with symptoms including weak acceleration, limp mode, whistling noises, and rising oil consumption.

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi L200 2.4 DI-D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 4N15 engine replaced the older 4D56 with a modern all-aluminium design, but it introduced its own set of common issues. These include exhaust manifold cracking, DPF regeneration problems causing oil dilution, and turbocharger failure. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Exhaust Manifold Cracking - The Most Common 4N15 Failure
problems.rootCause: The cooling system is believed to be undersized for the 4N15 engine, causing the exhaust manifold to operate at excessive temperatures which leads to cracking. Symptoms include loss of power, the engine entering limp mode, and audible exhaust leakage. Mitsubishi has released an updated manifold (part number 1555B029) to address this issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cracked manifold with updated part (1555B029), new gaskets, studs
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early; prevents power loss and further damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt 4N15 with updated manifold and cooling system components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If manifold failure has caused secondary turbo damage

problems.recommendation: If your L200 2.4 DI-D develops loss of power, limp mode, or a hissing/exhaust leak sound, have the exhaust manifold inspected immediately. If caught early, replacing the manifold with the updated part (1555B029) is significantly cheaper than a full engine rebuild. For vehicles with confirmed secondary damage to the turbocharger or engine, a rebuilt engine with updated components is the safest long-term solution.

problems.group: DPF Regeneration Failure and Oil Dilution
problems.h4: DPF Regeneration Failure and Oil Dilution
problems.rootCause: Frequent DPF regeneration cycles, particularly in urban or low-speed use, cause diesel fuel to dilute the engine oil. Owners have reported the DPF warning light illuminating every 2,000km, with engine oil level rising rapidly.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Forced DPF regeneration, oil and filter change with correct low-SAPS oil
repairOptions.longevity: Regular maintenance; essential for urban-driven examples

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace DPF filter, differential pressure sensor, oil and filter change
repairOptions.longevity: If DPF is blocked beyond regeneration

problems.recommendation: The 4N15 engine's DPF system is sensitive to short trips. If your L200 2.4 DI-D is used primarily for urban driving, schedule regular motorway runs (30+ minutes at 2,000+ rpm) to allow the DPF to regenerate properly. Use only the correct low-SAPS engine oil and change it at 6,000-8,000 mile intervals rather than the factory schedule. If the DPF warning light is frequent, have the system diagnosed to prevent oil dilution-related turbo and timing chain damage.

problems.rootCause: Turbocharger failure can be caused by oil supply issues, carbon buildup on VNT mechanisms, or damage from exhaust manifold debris. Symptoms include weak acceleration, limp mode, black/blue smoke, whistling noises, and rising oil consumption. In severe cases, metal debris can enter the intake and cause catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New or recon turbocharger (1515A417), oil feed line, oil and filter change
repairOptions.longevity: If caught before turbo debris has damaged the engine

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt 4N15 with new turbo and upgraded components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo debris has damaged pistons/cylinders

problems.recommendation: Turbo failure on the 4N15 is often linked to oil quality and service history. If your L200 2.4 DI-D develops turbo symptoms, have the turbocharger and oil supply system inspected immediately. If metal debris has circulated through the engine, a rebuilt engine with new turbo is recommended over partial repairs to avoid repeat failure.
